generatedProse.concept-context: Picture a seminar presentation on a psychology study. You decide your one message, perhaps what the study found and why it matters, then structure the talk around it and design slides that support it. The three ideas become one job, held together by what your audience needs to take away.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students present the same study to their seminar. One crams every result onto crowded slides and reads them out, with no single message, so the group loses the thread. The other picks one finding to build around, structures the talk clearly, and uses slides that show just the key graph. The second student's audience follows the study easily, because the parts worked as one practice.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, a presentation lands when its message, structure and slides pull the same way. You choose what the study shows, shape the talk around it, and let the slides back it up. Treated as one practice, the three ideas help your audience follow the psychology, not just the slides.

check.body: A student works out one clear message, plans an introduction, main body and conclusion around it, and builds slides that support it. The talk lands well. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That building a presentation works as one practice: the message, the structure and the slides all pulled the same way.
_items.feedback: Yes. The three parts worked together towards one clear message, which is the whole practice.

_items.text: That the slides were the only thing that mattered.
_items.feedback: The slides helped, but only because they supported a clear message and a sound structure.

_items.text: That the student was lucky, and planning made no difference.
_items.feedback: Planning shaped the talk. The parts working together are what made it land.

_items.text: That a clear message on its own is enough, without structure or slides.
_items.feedback: The message mattered, but the structure and slides carried it. All three worked together.
